title: Set floor monitors in each mic's null: cardioid 180 degrees, supercardioid 126
instruction: Sound check on a 1:10 stage: set one floor wedge for each seated singer in the null of her mic, so it will not feed back. The left singer's black cardioid mic: directly behind it, 180 degrees off the mic's front. The right singer's silver supercardioid: about 126 degrees off its front, either side. Stand each wedge base down 80 to 150 mm from its mic stand, its grey grille aimed at that singer's stool.
context: Audio and sound engineering technicians set floor monitors (wedges) on stage so performers hear themselves without feedback. A directional vocal mic is least sensitive in its null: a cardioid's is directly behind it, 180 degrees off its front axis, so its wedge goes straight behind the mic, aimed back at the singer; a supercardioid's nulls are about 126 degrees off its front on either side (it has a small rear lobe), so its wedge goes off to one side. Setting it straight behind out of habit is a classic sound-check mistake that costs gain before feedback. The wedge must also be aimed at the performer and stand at a usable distance (here 0.8 to 1.5 m). The null angles, applied seen from above, are those on microphone makers' monitor placement diagrams. The two singers here use different mics, so their wedges go in different places relative to their stands, and both wedges start in the wings facing the wrong way.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; the table top is the reference height. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up from the table top; the arm bases are at y +30.5 cm and y -30.5 cm. A 1:10 model of a small stage set for a seated acoustic duo, the audience on the arms' side (-x). (1) Stage deck: dark grey painted hardboard, 330 mm (along x) x 680 mm (along y) x 3 mm, fixed to the table, covering x 14.0 to 47.0 cm and y -34.0 to +34.0 cm; its top is the stage floor, 3 mm above the table. (2, 3) Stools: two round wooden stools 32 mm across and 45 mm tall (0.45 m seats), fixed on the deck, centred at x 43.0 cm, y +15.0 cm (the left singer's) and x 43.0 cm, y -15.0 cm (the right singer's). (4, 5) Mic stands: fixed on the deck 40 mm in front of the stools (toward the arms), centred at x 39.0 cm, y +15.0 cm (left) and x 39.0 cm, y -15.0 cm (right), black steel: a round base 30 mm across and 4 mm tall, a pole 8 mm across up to 104 mm above the table, a 14 x 14 x 6 mm clip on its top, and on the clip a metal vocal mic: a ball head 16 mm across centred straight above the pole, 115 mm above the deck (1.15 m, seated mouth height), and a 32 x 9 x 9 mm handle running from the back of the head toward the arms (-x). So each mic points straight upstage (+x), at its singer's stool. The left mic is a cardioid (black handle, dark grey head); the right mic is a supercardioid (silver handle and head). (6, 7) Floor wedges: two identical loose stage monitors, 80 g each, rigid: a black painted wooden cabinet 45 mm deep, 60 mm wide and 30 mm tall, stepped like a wedge's sloped front: a full-depth slab 12 mm tall and, at the back, a block 20 mm deep standing to the full 30 mm; a light grey steel-mesh grille 56 mm wide covers the step's top (25 mm deep, 2 mm thick) and the rear block's front face (2 mm thick, from 14 to 28 mm up). The grille faces the way the wedge sends its sound: forward, over its low front. 'The middle' of a wedge is the middle of its 45 x 60 mm footprint. Both wedges start in the wings, on the table off the deck, base down: the left one with its middle at x 22.0 cm, y +39.0 cm and its grille facing left (+y); the right one at x 22.0 cm, y -39.0 cm, its grille facing right (-y). Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: The score is read from the two wedges at the last step. Distances and angles are measured seen from above, from each mic stand's centre (its pole, straight under the mic's head). A wedge is 'placed' when all four hold: (a) its lowest point is within 3 mm of the deck's top; (b) it is base down, its up direction within 10 degrees of vertical (on its back, side, front or upside down it is placed nowhere); (c) its whole outline seen from above is over the deck; (d) it is at rest: neither the middle of its front face nor that of its back face moved more than 2 mm in the last 0.5 s. A placed wedge serves the singer whose mic stand is nearer its middle (the left singer on an exact tie). For that singer: r is the distance from her stand's centre to the wedge's middle; beta is the angle at the stand between the mic's front axis (straight upstage, +x, toward her stool) and the line to the wedge's middle, 0 to 180 degrees, on either side; her mic's null is 180 degrees for the left singer's cardioid and 126 degrees for the right singer's supercardioid (either side), and 'off the null' is the difference between beta and the null; 'aim' is the angle, seen from above, between the way the grille faces and the line from the wedge's middle to the centre of her stool. A singer scores 0.5 when a wedge serving her has r of 80 to 150 mm, is 15 degrees or less off the null and aimed within 20 degrees; 0.25 when one has r of 60 to 200 mm, is 30 degrees or less off the null and aimed within 45 degrees (and not 0.5); otherwise 0 (no placed wedge, or one beside or in front of the mic, too near or far, or not aimed at her). Two wedges serving one singer count once (the better). Score = left singer's + right singer's. Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0, and every outcome maps to exactly one: 1.0 both singers at 0.5; 0.75 one at 0.5 and the other at 0.25 (for example the right wedge 145 degrees round, 19 off its null, or the left wedge aimed 30 degrees off); 0.5 one at 0.5 and the other at 0 (for example both wedges straight behind their mics, the usual mistake: the supercardioid's wedge is then 54 degrees off its null), or both at 0.25; 0.25 one at 0.25 and the other at 0; 0 neither (wedges left in the wings, beside the mics, on their backs, held in the air). Set in the right places but unturned, as they were picked up, the wedges face the wings, aimed 90 and about 130 degrees off: 0. The trial ends early once 1.0 has held for 3 s. In a real trial a top photo, or a tape and a protractor centred on each stand's base, gives r, beta and aim, and a look from the side shows each wedge standing base down on the deck.
fidelity: Rigid bodies, default friction; the deck, stools and mic stands are fixed. No sound is simulated: the set-up is scored as a sound engineer checks it, by where each wedge stands and which way its grille faces, seen from above as on makers' placement diagrams (the mics' height above the wedges is not used). Each wedge is one rigid body of four boxes, its sloped front stepped. The scorer reads only the wedges, so a wedge still held but resting on the deck counts as set down.
reset_notes: Put the left wedge back in the left wing, on the table off the deck, base down, its middle at x 22.0 cm, y +39.0 cm, grille facing left (+y); and the right wedge at x 22.0 cm, y -39.0 cm, grille facing right (-y). The deck, stools and mic stands are fixed. Nothing is consumed.
